items.text:
Fils beat Jodar 4–6, 6–2, 6–2 in the group stage to get his first win at the ATP Finals and stay in contention for the semi-finals. It was the first appearance at this event for both players.

The first set could easily have gone the other way. Fils was the one with the break points but Jodar saved two of them early in the set and another one late. Then, in the very last game, Jodar broke to take it 6–4 and lead by a set. Fils was angry with himself for letting that set slip and the win brought him relief: "Here the first set was a bit so-so. I was struggling a little bit, a bit of frustration. … A little bit of relief now."

From there he took control. He broke early in the second set and won 5 games in a row to take it 6–2 and level at one set all. The deciding set went the same way. He got an early break, added a second one late and took it 6–2.

That turnaround came from the way he kept pressing to the end. He was clearly the better player from the baseline, hit his targets with real accuracy and kept putting Jodar's serve under pressure. Over the whole match, it added up to a dominance ratio of 1.66.

On the other side of the net, Jodar called the physio in the middle of the second set.

That is a good win with one clear thing to fix. Fils landed only 50% of his first serves, well below his 63% average on hard and he will need more of them in his last group match. Up next: Zverev.

Fils: performance rating 8.8 | W: 18 / UE: 19 | DR: 1.66

Jodar: performance rating 7.6 | W: 20 / UE: 33 | DR: 0.60

items.text:
Shelton beat Fils in three sets at the ATP Finals in Turin, his first ever match win at this event. It was also the first appearance here for Fils and he made Shelton fight all the way to a deciding set.

From the start Shelton was the stronger player. Fils had to save 4 break points just to hold early on and the breaks came soon after that. Shelton won 5 games in a row to take the first set 6–2 and lead by a set. The second set went the other way. Fils broke late, served for the set and held on to take it 6–3 for one set all.

That left everything to the third set and Fils came into it slowly. He knew it and was not happy with himself: "It's a shame that I started the third set with the handbrake slightly on … I'm staying positive ahead of the next matches" Shelton made him pay right away. He needed 4 break points in the opening return game but got the break for 2–0. A few games later Fils had 2 chances to break back. Shelton saved both and held for 4–1. He stayed calm when he served for the match, saved one more break point and took the set 6–3.

items.text:
Zverev beat Jodar in straight sets in the opening singles match of the week in Turin. It was the first appearance at this event for Jodar, who is only 20.

The first set stayed even until the middle. Jodar saved two break points to hold and Zverev broke him soon after. Then Zverev served for the set and fell behind 15–40 but he saved both break points and took it 6–4. The second set followed the same pattern. Zverev broke early and did not see another break point. Jodar saved three more break points late in the set to stay close but Zverev served it out 6–4. Jodar afterwards: "He handled the important points better than I did … I don't feel pressure, I try to enjoy it as much as possible"

The score was kinder to Jodar than the match itself, because he kept it close only by saving 5 of 7 break points. Jodar never got a real look at the first serve. Zverev won 86% of the points behind it, far above his 74% average on hard.

A very good start to the week from Zverev, a clean and dominant win with a dominance ratio of 2.01. He handled the important points better than the young debutant and was never in real danger. Shelton waits next.
